QUESTION 1 OF 5

Main Objective & Real-World Problem Solved

CORE VISION

🛑 The Real-World Pain Points

  • •
    Microservice Sprawl & Ingress Chaos: Clients interacting directly with backend services suffer from tight coupling, exposed ports, and duplicated auth logic across every repo.
  • •
    Failures of "Dumb" Load Balancing: Standard round-robin blindly pushes traffic to servers with high latency or exhausted thread pools, causing cascading cluster outages.
  • •
    Reactive Rate Limiting: Standard rate limiters only kick in after a server is already failing under sudden surges or volumetric DDoS attacks.

🎯 Nexus Gateway's Solved State

  • ✔
    Unified Zero-Trust Edge: Centralized Netty reverse proxy validates stateless HMAC-SHA256 JWTs and propagates identities downstream.
  • ✔
    Smart Health-Weighted Routing: Algorithm scores instances by latency, CPU, and errors, routing only to optimal servers.
  • ✔
    Proactive AI Traffic Shaping: ML pipeline projects traffic 10 minutes in advance and automatically injects Redis throttling rules.
INNOVATION MATRIX

System Innovations & Measurable Value

BENCHMARKS
01

Sub-50ms Gateway Ingress

Non-blocking asynchronous Netty event loops minimize proxy latency. Logging is fire-and-forget to Kafka, ensuring audit trails never block response delivery.

02

Zero-Downtime Policy Tuning

Operators and AI models can inject live rate limits per IP, User UUID, or Global traffic directly into Redis with automatic TTL expiration—no server reboots required.

03

High Availability Pairing

All high-traffic microservices deploy in dual-replica pairs (e.g. user-service-1 & 2). If a replica experiences degradation, traffic instantly shifts 100% to its peer.

QUESTION 2 OF 5

Technology Stack Justification & Rationale

ENGINEERING CHOICES
Spring Cloud Gateway (Netty) EDGE GATEWAY

Reactive non-blocking I/O powered by Project Reactor. Handles tens of thousands of concurrent connections with low memory footprint compared to thread-per-request Tomcat servlets.

Apache Kafka 7.5 & Zookeeper EVENT BROKER

Enterprise event streaming handling 100,000+ msgs/sec. Decouples request logging from the gateway's critical path, completely eliminating database write bottlenecks.

Redis 7 (In-Memory Engine) CACHE & THROTTLING

Sub-millisecond latency for distributed token-bucket counters (100 RPM limit) and transient policy overrides backed by native key expiration (TTL).

FastAPI + Scikit-Learn AI PREDICTION

Python ecosystem enables state-of-the-art RandomForest regression for 10-minute traffic load forecasting and IsolationForest for multivariate anomaly and outlier detection.

QUESTION 3 (CONT.)

End-to-End Ingress Request Lifecycle

6-STEP FLOW
Step 1: Ingress Route Match

Client calls Gateway at /api/*. Gateway matches route predicates and strips prefixes for downstream routing.

Step 2: Stateless JWT Filter

Validates Bearer token signature. Rejects unauthorized calls with 401; mutates request headers with user claims.

Step 3: Redis Rate Limiting

Token bucket evaluates IP/User request counts. If quota exceeded, short-circuits with 429 Too Many Requests.

Step 4: Smart Instance Routing

Calculates health scores across instance pairs and forwards request to the healthiest available node.

Step 5: Upstream Processing

Microservice executes business logic against PostgreSQL using UUID keys and returns response payload.

Step 6: Async Kafka Stream

Gateway logs latency and metadata to Kafka topic api-log-events; log-consumer updates ML models.

QUESTION 3 (ALGORITHMS)

Smart Routing Formula & Machine Learning

AI ENGINE

Dynamic Health Score Algorithm

Health Score = 0.5(Latency) + 0.3(CPU) + 0.2(Errors)
  • Latency (50%): Normalized inverse response time (<50ms = 100).
  • CPU (30%): Actuator metrics inverse utilization.
  • Errors (20%): Proportion of 2xx/3xx vs 4xx/5xx responses.
  • Automatic Shift: If node score drops <40, 100% traffic fails over.

Dual Machine Learning Models

1. RandomForestRegressor (Traffic Horizon) Models nonlinear historical traffic patterns to project request rates 10 minutes in advance with overload probabilities.
2. IsolationForest (Unsupervised Outliers) Detects multi-dimensional anomalies (Z-score latency surges, unusual request burst densities, DDoS patterns).
QUESTION 4 OF 5

Major Technical Challenges & Solutions

DEBUGGING & FIXES
Challenge 1: Reactive WebFlux vs. ThreadLocal

Gateway runs Netty event loops where requests hop worker threads. ThreadLocal security context was lost.

✔ Resolution

Mutated ServerWebExchange reactive headers directly (X-User-Id, X-User-Role), eliminating ThreadLocal dependencies.

Challenge 2: Synchronous DB Logging Bottleneck

Direct DB logging spiked gateway latency from 15ms to over 1,200ms due to connection pool exhaustion.

✔ Resolution

Deployed Apache Kafka pipeline: gateway publishes log events asynchronously in memory buffer, zero client wait.

Challenge 3: UUIDv4 Migration Frontend Parsing Bug

Switching from integer IDs to UUIDv4 caused parseInt() NaN errors on payment and notification dispatches.

✔ Resolution

Updated backend DTOs to java.util.UUID and implemented dynamic user selectors in the React dashboard.

QUESTION 5 OF 5

Key System Limitations

CONSTRAINTS
1. Single-Broker Infrastructure

Current setup deploys single instances of Redis and Kafka. While suitable for single-region clusters, it represents a single point of failure (SPOF) compared to multi-broker Kafka partitions.

2. ML Cold-Start Horizon

Scikit-Learn regression models rely on historical rolling traffic. During the first 5 minutes after a cold reboot, forecast confidence intervals are wider until baseline traffic is sampled.

3. Coarse-Grained Token Cost

Every HTTP request decrements the token bucket by 1 token regardless of computational weight (a lightweight health ping costs the same as a heavy SQL search aggregation).

4. Internal Transport Unencrypted

Communication between the gateway and internal microservices uses plain HTTP inside the Docker bridge network rather than mutual TLS (mTLS).
